focus: Rwanda tax-benefit surface: employment income tax (PAYE) and the lump-sum regime, rental income tax, RSSB contributions (pension, occupational hazards, maternity leave, and the RAMA and MMI medical schemes), community-based health insurance (CBHI) contributions, VAT, excise duty, and the VUP Direct Support, school feeding, Girinka and fuel-subsidy programmes. The wired RWAMOD suites compare PAYE, the lump-sum tax, rental income tax, the pension, maternity, RAMA and MMI contributions, the CBHI member premiums, VAT, three excise rows, and a formal private-sector worker's monthly disposable income with its CBHI levy.
purpose: Household-level comparison-oracle and supporting-source references for Rwanda Axiom coverage. None of these are legal authority.
oracle_scope: A RuleSpec oracle must be an executable, pinned external calculator that accepts household-level inputs and returns household-level tax-benefit outputs comparable to Axiom outputs. Aggregate simulators, distributional reports, parameter documentation, and public model summaries are supporting references only, not oracles.

oracles.name: RWAMOD
oracles.dataset: rw_2024_a1 (registered dataset name only; the bundle ships no Rwandan microdata, so the suites run a header-only input file and every comparison household is synthetic; no survey data is used)
oracles.role: Household-level tax-benefit comparison oracle for Rwanda, wired through per-case suites in axiom-oracles (see wired). RWAMOD is the SOUTHMOD tax-benefit microsimulation model for Rwanda (UNU-WIDER), built on the EUROMOD platform.

availability_check.detail: UNU-WIDER approved Axiom's SOUTHMOD access request on 2026-07-07. RWAMOD is part of the SOUTHMOD A4.0 bundle (sha256 in bundle_sha256), held locally under the SOUTHMOD_A4.0 Adhesion Agreement (personal links; non-redistributable; never committed or shared). Under footnote 2 of the agreement UNU-WIDER provides only Stata do-files for RWAMOD's input data, so the bundle ships no Rwandan microdata and every comparison household is synthetic. RWAMOD is wired as the Rwanda household oracle by eight per-case comparison suites in TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-oracles (comparisons/rw-*.yaml, axiom-oracles#260), run on system RW_2025 through scripts/run_comparison.py on the licensed machine. They are manual-lane suites (ci: manual): clause 4 of the agreement bars giving the bundle or its input data to any third party, so they never run on shared CI runners. On 2026-10-04, against rulespec-rw 001fa4b and axiom-rules-engine 6f62c12: 42 cases, 64 comparisons, 64 matched and 0 dispositioned, every comparison within the suites' 1-FRW tolerance (largest difference 0.3 FRW). The Axiom side evaluates period 2026 in seven suites, whose configs record that every compared schedule is value-identical across 2025 and 2026, and period 2027 in rw-cbhi-tiers (see its note). Oracle-side findings are recorded in axiom-oracles axiom_oracles/data/rwamod_issues.json. rulespec-rw has no .axiom/encoding-manifests/, so none of the modules these suites compare carries an encoding manifest or is attested supervised-encoder output (rulespec-rw#18 item 1); the comparisons should be re-run after the supervised re-encode.

oracles.systems: RW_2025 (CY2025), the system every wired suite runs (see wired)
oracles.acknowledgement: Results are based on the tax-benefit microsimulation model for Rwanda (RWAMOD) in SOUTHMOD_A4.0, developed, maintained and managed by UNU-WIDER with SASPRI, the LSE International Inequalities Institute and local partners, run on the EUROMOD software (EM_Executable 1.0.0 via the euromod connector 0.2.18) under the registered rw_2024_a1 dataset name; the bundle ships no Rwandan microdata, so a header-only input file is built locally from the model's own variable list and every household is synthetic. The results and their interpretation are Axiom's responsibility.

wired.dataset_configuration: rw_2024_a1 (registered dataset name only; the bundle ships no Rwandan microdata, so runs use a header-only input file and every comparison household is synthetic)

suites.note: Period-shifted schedule check: the Axiom side runs period 2027 because Ministerial Order No 002/26/10/TC starts on 2026-02-23, against RW_2025, so a match confirms the schedule amounts, not CY2025 law (ledger rwamod-cbhi-tier-premiums-gazetting-timing). The suite chooses the social-registry level paired with each case; no committed source maps incomes to registry levels.

The levy comparison tests the composed pipeline's own copy of the CBHI levy rate, not the PM Order No 105/03 module (rulespec-rw#18 item 2), and for the 2026 period the suite evaluates that rate rests on a repealed Order (item 3).

Compares three Annex rows only. The cigarette retail value is RWAMOD's own expenditure base, bridged under a parity convention (ledger rwamod-expenditure-read-tax-inclusive-for-excise-pre-tax-for-vat), so that row tests the rate and per-pack amount, not the base; uncompared rows carry ledger findings rwamod-water-excise-row-repealed, rwamod-juice-basket-local-rate and rwamod-beer-fermented-basket-rates.

Rate check on one food item: the taxable value is RWAMOD's own VAT base, bridged under a parity convention (ledger rwamod-expenditure-read-tax-inclusive-for-excise-pre-tax-for-vat), so the suite tests the standard rate, not the base definition. VAT on excisable purchases and the bottled-water item is not compared (ledger rwamod-bottled-water-vat-charged-twice).
